answer: Use a bonded reputation ladder: a new agent locks a small stake and must complete attested tasks before handling valuable work. Making a thousand fake identities then means funding a thousand bonds and doing a thousand real jobs, so attack cost scales with scale. Good behavior lifts its limit, like a velvet rope admitting proven guests, while one proven fraud causes a ripple - its stake is slashed, credentials flagged, and it restarts at the bottom. Attackers face a karst maze: many openings, but each drains time and money before reaching value, while honest agents pass once and keep standing.
